PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request for the continued operation of an existing wireless
telecommunications facility for a period of 10 years located at 1233 West Rancho Vista
Boulevard. The facility was previously approved as a 39-foot sign structure of the
Antelope Valley (AV) Mall, that later had a substantial modification to increase the height
to 50-feet and locate a wireless telecommunication facility within the existing sign
structure located on the northwest corner of West Rancho Vista Boulevard and 10th Street
West.

BACKGROUND

On September 7, 2000, the Planning Commission approved CUP 00-05 (Resolution No.
PC-2000-035), which allowed for the increase in height of the existing 39-foot-high sign
structure of the AV Mall, located on the northwest corner of West Rancho Vista Boulevard
and 10th Street West, by 11-feet in order to install a wireless telecommunications facility
with a 273 square foot utility building.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.A, major wireless
telecommunications facilities expire after a period of 10 years, unless a time extension is
approved. Since a time extension application was not received prior to expiration of the
wireless telecommunications facility, the entitlement expired, and a new CUP is required
for the continued operation of the facility.

The existing facility has been modified four times since the original approval, through the
following Minor Modifications (MM):

    MM 06-35 approved on August 17, 2006;
    MM 13-071 approved on January 15, 2015;
    MM 14-017 approved on June 7, 2016;
    MM 16-003 approved on February 22, 2016; and,
    MM 19-035 approved on July 22, 2019.

The subject application was submitted on August 30, 2023, and was deemed complete
and scheduled for the November 9, 2023, Planning Commission meeting.

Design

The existing wireless telecommunications facility complies with the design standards
found within PMC Section 17.95.030.B, because all antennas are concealed within the
AV Mall sign structure, and the equipment is located within a neutral-colored enclosure

Access

For ongoing maintenance purposes, the project will continue to take access from Mall
Ring Road, west of 10th Street West. Additionally, the site has adequate parking for
maintenance vehicles adjacent to the facility. The existing facility has ladders built into
the interior of the monument structure to allow access to the antennas for the majority of
maintenance. When significant maintenance is required, the applicant will utilize a boom
lift and implement traffic control measures to access antennas.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
An Initial Study was prepared for the project in conjunction with the original approval and
on September 7, 2000, the Planning Commission adopted an MND finding that, with the
incorporation of mitigation measures, the project would not have a significant impact on
the environment. Staff has reviewed the MND to determine whether the project triggered
any of the conditions described in Sections 15162, 15163, and 15164 of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines and determined that additional
documentation is not required for the project because CUP 23-0013 does not propose
any significant revisions to the project, there are no changes in circumstances and there
is no new information of substantial importance that will involve new significant
environmental effects or increase the severity of previously identified significant effects.
The proposed project is a request for the continued operation of an existing wireless
telecommunications facility for a period of 10 years and does not include any alterations
to the facility as approved through CUP 00-05. Furthermore, a Radio Frequency report
was submitted as part of the mitigation monitoring program and shows that the project
will continue to be compliant with Federal Communications Commission rules and
regulations, as described in the Office of Engineering and Technology Bulletin 65.

OPTIONS

The Planning Commission has the following options:

1.  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-025 approving CUP 23-0013 and find that the
  project is consistent with the previously adopted MND and MMRP.

2.  Continue the project and direct staff to return with additional information.

3.  Deny the project.

Option 1 is recommended.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct seven residential buildings, one mixed-use building,
and associated outdoor recreation spaces in two phases located west of 30th Street East
and approximately 1,000 feet south of Palmdale Boulevard. The seven townhouse
buildings will each include two four-bedroom units with a connected studio unit. The
residential portion of the site also includes play areas for multiple age ranges, picnic and
outdoor event areas, and a garden. The mixed-use area will be located along
30th Street East and will include six affordable studio units, 2,800 square feet of office
space, 4,200 square feet of community space, and outdoor event and picnic areas, which
are allowed uses within the Mixed Use 1 (MU 1) zone. The project is intended to provide
housing for foster care youth, onsite resource caregivers, and family members.

The project will be a phased development: Phase 1 will include the construction of the
community center, six townhouse buildings (12 units), and two studio apartments, and
Phase 2 will include the construction of one additional townhouse building and four studio
apartments.

The proposed project also includes PD 23-001, a request for approval of a document that
allows flexibility of development standards.

The subject application was submitted on April 12, 2023, and deemed incomplete. After
resolution of completeness items, the project was deemed complete on
October 10, 2023, and scheduled for the November 9, 2023, Planning Commission
meeting.

ARCHITECTURE

Aside from the proposed deviations within PD 23-001, the project complies with all
requirements of the City of Palmdale s Multi-Family and Mixed-Use Design Standards,
which were adopted to provide objective design standards for all multi-family and mixed-
use projects. The proposed project will include various building materials and textures,
including acrylic-based plaster, non-reflective metal, perforated metal, gabion rock walls,
and a standing seam metal roof. In addition, the design includes earth tones which are
compatible with the desert environment and opportunities for painted murals.
Furthermore, architectural enhancements such as varying roof lines, building projections,
and entrance courtyards will be provided on the front and rear of the building, clearly
denoting the main entrances. In addition, Conditions of Approval for this project have
been included to ensure that all equipment is adequately screened from public view.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is Categorically Exempt from California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) review pursuant to Section 15332, Class 32, Infill Development, of the CEQA
Guidelines, which exempts in-fill development projects that have no significant impacts to
the environment. The project qualifies as in-fill development because it consists of the
construction of seven residential buildings, one mixed-use building including residential,
community, and office uses, and outdoor event spaces on a site within the MU 1 (Mixed
Use 1) zone, which allows the proposed uses. In addition, the project occurs within the
City, on a site of less than five acres, and is substantially surrounded by urban uses with
commercial development to the north, residential development to the east, and a City
park to the south. In addition, the vacant parcels to the west of the subject site have been
highly disturbed by vehicular and human activity.

OPTIONS

The Planning Commission has the following options:

1.  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2023-022 recommending City Council approval of
  PD 23-001, approving SPR 23-003, and find that the project is categorically
  exempt from environmental review.

2.  Continue the project and direct staff to return with additional information.

3.  Deny the project.

Option 1 is recommended.

 Villages, a development of foster care housing, and associated uses. The Project will be designed to create a village-like housing development to
 provide stable housing for foster youth and allow siblings to stay together in the same home. In addition to the seven two-unit townhouse buildings, the
 project will also include a mixed-use building which will include office space, six studio units, and a community center to be used for the foster youth and
 the community.
 The combination of the above site elements will be enhanced with amenities, which include a generous landscaped area which will include play areas for
 multiple age-ranges, picnic and outdoor event areas, and a garden. The mixed-use area will also include picnic and outdoor events areas, and a desert
 plan garden along 30th Street East. This Planned Development will result in a high quality, efficient, and thoughtfully designed mixed use development
 (Mixed Use 1 MU 1) which will bring in needed foster youth housing and services to the Antelope Valley.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request to amend Title 17 of the Palmdale Municipal Code
(PMC) to update definitions and clarify review procedures.

BACKGROUND

On September 21, 2022, Palmdale 2045 was adopted by the City Council and replaced
the previously adopted General Plan (1993). State law requires that the regulations
governing the use and development of lands within the municipal limits of a city be
consistent with the adopted General Plan for that city. ZOA 21-007 was adopted by the
City Council on March 15, 2023, which amended Title 17 of the PMC to implement the
vision of Palmdale 2045 as well as support new land use patterns and future
development. Ordinance No. 1614 was adopted by the City Council on August 16, 2023,
which included minor amendments to Title 17 necessary to address inconsistencies,
clarify review procedures, correct typographical errors and section references, as well as
update the associated Zoning Map. Since then, City staff has identified minor
amendments necessary to update definitions and clarify review procedures.

ANALYSIS

    Clarify the definition of drive-through services and restaurant facility
